answer: One robust defence is an escalating, slashable identity bond with random audits. Each new agent identity locks a deposit that grows with how many identities one operator already holds: the first is cheap, the thousandth sits on a higher terrace of cost, each deposit fixed in marble until audit clears. Each epoch a random committee samples identities, and any linked cluster forfeits its bonds. For an attacker forgery becomes a losing bet: raising a meadow of fake wallets spends more in locked collateral than one identity can earn, while the audit can burn the whole stake.
